before.name: Phosphorylation
before.tldr: Adding phosphate can change a protein’s behavior in several ways. The site and cellular context determine whether a measured change indicates activation, inhibition or something else.
before.summary: Protein kinases commonly transfer phosphate from ATP to a substrate, producing ADP. Protein phosphatases remove phosphate by hydrolysis without regenerating ATP. A modification can affect catalysis, binding, localization or interactions; sites on one protein can have different functions. Src experiments demonstrated an inhibitory tail-phosphorylation mechanism in their defined preparation, so phosphorylation should not be treated as universal activation.

links.label: Dephosphorylation or antibody binding to the carboxy terminus stimulates pp60c-src.
Ischemia in tumors induces early and sustained phosphorylation changes in stress kinase pathways but does not affect global protein levels.

notes: A phosphosite signal depends on modified molecules, parent-protein amount, recovery and measurement. It is not automatically site occupancy, the fraction modified at that site. A parent-normalized ratio may be informative without becoming an absolute occupancy percentage. Retain site identity/localization confidence, method, specimen handling and time.

This modifies existing molecules and is distinct from changing DNA sequence, RNA production or mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation. One site alone need not identify the responsible enzyme or the state of a whole pathway.

In a fictional comparison, sample A has a phosphopeptide signal of 1 and a parent-protein signal of 1; sample B has signals of 2 and 2 on the same relative scale. Both ratios are 1, so the doubled phosphopeptide signal alone does not establish an increased modified fraction. Comparable recovery and measurement are assumed; these ratios are neither absolute molecule counts nor calibrated occupancy percentages. In a separate serine-site example, a kinase transfers phosphate from ATP to the site's oxygen and makes ADP. A phosphatase uses water to release phosphate and restore the hydroxyl group, without making ATP. These reactions modify a site on an existing molecule and do not measure how much protein is present.

before.name: Receptor
before.tldr: Receptors connect molecular recognition to a cellular response through several mechanisms. Their presence and their activity are separate findings.
before.summary: Receptors can be on the surface or inside a cell. Ligand-gated ion channels regulate ion passage; G-protein-coupled receptors act through G proteins; enzyme-linked receptors can contain an enzyme or recruit a separate one. Intracellular nuclear receptors can regulate transcription with cellular partners. A surface signal can ultimately alter genes, while nuclear-receptor family membership does not fix every molecule permanently in the nucleus or require every effect to use new transcription.

links.label: Cell membrane and nuclear estrogen receptors (ERs) originate from a single transcript: studies of ERalpha and ERbeta expressed in Chinese hamster ovary cells.
Diwanji et al.: HER2-HER3-neuregulin structural complexes (2021)
Diwanji et al.: corrected figure labels and residue numbering (2022)

notes: Defined engineered estrogen-receptor experiments detected nuclear and membrane pools; they do not establish a universal proportion in human tumors. Distinguish receptor identity, location, accessible binding and measured function. A positive stain or fluorescence intensity is not automatically a calibrated receptor count, pathway dependence or drug sensitivity.

HER2 is an orphan receptor without a known direct activating ligand. Its partner HER3 binds neuregulin. Diwanji and colleagues studied the HER2-HER3-NRG1-beta complex, including defined mutant and purified-complex experiments, so a generic growth factor drawn directly on HER2 would assign the wrong binding partner. Antibody binding, disruption of an assembled complex and inhibition of activation are separate outcomes; the mutant-complex results do not define every antibody response in an unmodified tumour.

In a selected cell-edge example, a G-protein-coupled receptor binds a ligand outside the cell and couples to a G protein on the cytoplasmic side. A separate ligand-gated channel has a ligand-binding site and a pore for ions; the chosen open state and inward arrow do not make every binding event open a channel or determine every ion's direction. A hypothetical probe that remains outside can reach an exposed binding site, while a different entering ligand can reach an intracellular receptor and, in a selected route, influence nuclear gene regulation. These are examples of access and relay, not an exhaustive receptor taxonomy or a universal permeability rule. They do not measure receptor abundance, growth dependence or treatment benefit.
